title: BLR soundness over a prime field
statement:
Let $p$ be prime and fix $n \ge 0$. Let $f : \bbz_p^n \to \bbz_p$ be a normalized function (so $f(0)=0$), and let $0 \le \varepsilon \le 1$ be such that $f$ is $\varepsilon$-far from every linear map, meaning $\mathrm{dist}(f,g) \ge \varepsilon$ for every linear $g : \bbz_p^n \to \bbz_p$, where $\mathrm{dist}(f,g) = \Pr_x[f(x) \ne g(x)]$. Then the BLR acceptance probability of $f$ satisfies
\[
  \Pr_{x,y}\bigl[f(x+y) = f(x)+f(y)\bigr]
  \;\le\; 1 - \frac{p-1}{p}\,\bigl(1 - \cos(2\pi/p)\bigr)\,\varepsilon,
\]
where $x,y$ range uniformly and independently over $\bbz_p^n$.
hypotheses_covered: f is ε-far from every linear function (dist(f,g) ≥ ε for all linear g)
replaced:
